solution: Write each root in terms of \(i\): \(\sqrt{-16} = 4i\), \(\sqrt{-25} = 5i\), \(\sqrt{-36} = 6i\), \(\sqrt{-625} = 25i\). The expression becomes \(4i + 3(5i) + 6i - 25i = (4 + 15 + 6 - 25)i\). Answer: \(0\)
Here \(\sqrt{-4} = 2i\), \(\sqrt{-9} = 3i\) and \(\sqrt{-16} = 4i\), so the expression is \(4(2i) + 5(3i) - 3(4i) = 8i + 15i - 12i\). Answer: \(11i\)
The conjugate of \(a + ib\) is \(a - ib\), so only the sign of the imaginary part changes. Answer: \(3 - i\)
Changing the sign of the imaginary part of \(3 - i\) gives the conjugate. Answer: \(3 + i\)
Here \(a = -\sqrt{5}\) and \(b = -\sqrt{7}\); the real part is unchanged and the imaginary part changes sign. Answer: \(-\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{7}\,i\)
First put it in \(a + ib\) form: \(-\sqrt{-5} = -\sqrt{5}\,i = 0 - \sqrt{5}\,i\). Changing the sign of the imaginary part gives the conjugate. Answer: \(\sqrt{5}\,i\)
\(5i = 0 + 5i\), so its conjugate is \(0 - 5i\). Answer: \(-5i\)
The imaginary part of \(\sqrt{5} - i\) is \(-1\); changing its sign gives the conjugate. Answer: \(\sqrt{5} + i\)
The imaginary part of \(\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{3}\,i\) is \(\sqrt{3}\); changing its sign gives the conjugate. Answer: \(\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{3}\,i\)
Here the real part is \(\cos\theta\) and the imaginary part is \(\sin\theta\); changing the sign of the imaginary part gives the conjugate. Answer: \(\cos\theta - i\sin\theta\)

Two complex numbers are equal only if their real and imaginary parts are separately equal. Imaginary parts: \(2a = 6\), so \(a = 3\). Real parts: \(a + 2b = 4\), so \(3 + 2b = 4\) and \(b = \dfrac{1}{2}\). Answer: \(a = 3\), \(b = \dfrac{1}{2}\)
Equating real parts: \(a - b = a\), so \(b = 0\). Equating imaginary parts: \(a + b = 5\), so \(a = 5\). Answer: \(a = 5\), \(b = 0\)

The left side is \((a+b)(2+i) = 2(a+b) + (a+b)i\). Equating real parts: \(2a + 2b = b + 1\), i.e. \(2a + b = 1\). Equating imaginary parts: \(a + b = 10 + 2a\), i.e. \(b = 10 + a\). Substituting, \(2a + (10 + a) = 1\), so \(3a = -9\). Answer: \(a = -3\), \(b = 7\)

Write the equation as \(0 + abi = (3a - b) + 12i\). Equating real parts: \(3a - b = 0\), so \(b = 3a\). Equating imaginary parts: \(ab = 12\), so \(a(3a) = 12\), giving \(a^2 = 4\) and \(a = \pm 2\), with \(b = 3a\) taking the matching sign. Answer: \(a = 2, b = 6\) or \(a = -2, b = -6\)

Taking reciprocals, \(a + ib = \dfrac{1}{3 - 2i} = \dfrac{3 + 2i}{3^2 + 2^2} = \dfrac{3 + 2i}{13}\). Comparing real and imaginary parts gives the values. Answer: \(a = \dfrac{3}{13}\), \(b = \dfrac{2}{13}\)

First simplify the denominator: \((3-i)(1+2i) = 3 + 6i - i - 2i^2 = 5 + 5i\). So the expression is \(\dfrac{2+i}{5(1+i)} = \dfrac{(2+i)(1-i)}{5 \times 2} = \dfrac{2 - 2i + i + 1}{10} = \dfrac{3 - i}{10}\). Answer: \(\dfrac{3}{10} - \dfrac{1}{10}i\), so \(a = \dfrac{3}{10}\) and \(b = -\dfrac{1}{10}\)
First, \(\dfrac{1+i}{1-i} = \dfrac{(1+i)^2}{(1-i)(1+i)} = \dfrac{2i}{2} = i\). Squaring gives \(i^2 = -1\). Answer: \(-1 + 0i\), so \(a = -1\) and \(b = 0\)

The two terms are conjugates of each other, so their sum is twice the real part of the first. Now \(\dfrac{3+2i}{2-5i} = \dfrac{(3+2i)(2+5i)}{2^2 + 5^2} = \dfrac{6 + 19i - 10}{29} = \dfrac{-4 + 19i}{29}\), so the sum is \(2 \times \left(-\dfrac{4}{29}\right)\). Answer: \(-\dfrac{8}{29} + 0i\), so \(a = -\dfrac{8}{29}\) and \(b = 0\)

Since \(\sqrt{-3} = \sqrt{3}\,i\), the expression is \(\dfrac{2 + \sqrt{3}\,i}{4 + \sqrt{3}\,i}\). Multiplying above and below by \(4 - \sqrt{3}\,i\): numerator \(= 8 - 2\sqrt{3}\,i + 4\sqrt{3}\,i + 3 = 11 + 2\sqrt{3}\,i\), denominator \(= 16 + 3 = 19\). Answer: \(\dfrac{11}{19} + \dfrac{2\sqrt{3}}{19}i\), so \(a = \dfrac{11}{19}\) and \(b = \dfrac{2\sqrt{3}}{19}\)

Convert each part: \(2\sqrt{-4} = 4i\), \(\sqrt{-9} = 3i\), and \((2+3i)(2-3i) = 2^2 - (3i)^2 = 4 + 9 = 13\). So the expression is \(\left(-\sqrt{5} + 4i\right) + \left(1 - 3i\right) + 13 = \left(-\sqrt{5} + 1 + 13\right) + (4 - 3)i\). Answer: \(\left(14 - \sqrt{5}\right) + 1i\), so \(a = 14 - \sqrt{5}\) and \(b = 1\)
This is a product of conjugates: \((2+3i)(2-3i) = 2^2 - (3i)^2 = 4 - 9i^2 = 4 + 9\). Answer: \(13 + 0i\), so \(a = 13\) and \(b = 0\)

First square: \(\left(-1 + \sqrt{3}\,i\right)^2 = 1 - 2\sqrt{3}\,i + 3i^2 = -2 - 2\sqrt{3}\,i\). Now multiply by \(-1 + \sqrt{3}\,i\): \(\left(-2 - 2\sqrt{3}\,i\right)\left(-1 + \sqrt{3}\,i\right) = 2 - 2\sqrt{3}\,i + 2\sqrt{3}\,i - 6i^2 = 2 + 6\). The imaginary part is \(0\), so the cube is real. Answer: \(8\), a real number
\(35 = 4(8) + 3\), so \(i^{35} = \left(i^4\right)^8 \times i^3 = 1 \times i^3\). Answer: \(-i\)
\(888 = 4(222)\) leaves remainder \(0\), so \(i^{888} = \left(i^4\right)^{222}\). Answer: \(1\)
\(116 = 4(29)\) leaves remainder \(0\), so \(i^{116} = \left(i^4\right)^{29}\). Answer: \(1\)

Reduce the powers: \(i^{10} = i^2 = -1\), \(i^{20} = \left(i^4\right)^5 = 1\), \(i^{30} = i^2 = -1\). So the expression is \(1 - 1 + 1 - 1 = 0\), and its imaginary part is \(0\), so it lies in \(\mathbb{R}\). Answer: \(0\), a real number

Take the lowest power out of each row: numerator \(= i^{584}\left(i^8 + i^6 + i^4 + i^2 + 1\right)\) and denominator \(= i^{574}\left(i^8 + i^6 + i^4 + i^2 + 1\right)\). The common bracket equals \(1 - 1 + 1 - 1 + 1 = 1 \ne 0\), so it cancels, leaving \(i^{584 - 574} = i^{10} = i^2\). Answer: \(-1\)

The exponents are \(0, 2, 4, \ldots, 20\), which is \(11\) terms, and \(i^{2k} = \left(i^2\right)^k = (-1)^k\). So the sum is \(1 - 1 + 1 - 1 + \cdots + 1\) with six terms \(+1\) and five terms \(-1\). Answer: \(1\)
Reduce the powers: \(i^{10} = i^2 = -1\), \(i^{100} = \left(i^4\right)^{25} = 1\), \(i^{1000} = \left(i^4\right)^{250} = 1\). So the expression is \(1 + (-1) + 1 - 1 = 0\), as required. Answer: \(0\)

Each exponent leaves remainder \(2\) on division by \(4\): \(i^{14} = i^{18} = i^{22} = i^2 = -1\). So the expression is \(1 - 1 - 1 - 1 = -2\), whose imaginary part is \(0\). Answer: Yes, it is a real number; its value is \(-2 \in \mathbb{R}\)
First, \(1 + \dfrac{1}{i} = 1 + \dfrac{i}{i^2} = 1 - i\). So the product is \((1+i)^4(1-i)^4 = \left[(1+i)(1-i)\right]^4 = \left(1 - i^2\right)^4 = 2^4\). Answer: \(16\), as required
Numerator: \(i^6 + i^7 + i^8 + i^9 = -1 - i + 1 + i = 0\). Denominator: \(i^2 + i^3 = -1 - i \ne 0\). So the value is \(\dfrac{0}{-1-i}\). Answer: \(0\)

\(a^2 = \left(\dfrac{-1 + \sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1 - 2\sqrt{3}\,i + 3i^2}{4} = \dfrac{-2 - 2\sqrt{3}\,i}{4} = \dfrac{-1 - \sqrt{3}\,i}{2} = b\). Similarly \(b^2 = \dfrac{1 + 2\sqrt{3}\,i + 3i^2}{4} = \dfrac{-2 + 2\sqrt{3}\,i}{4} = \dfrac{-1 + \sqrt{3}\,i}{2} = a\). Answer: \(a^2 = b\) and \(b^2 = a\)

Expand the cube: \((a + ib)^3 = a^3 + 3a^2(ib) + 3a(ib)^2 + (ib)^3 = \left(a^3 - 3ab^2\right) + \left(3a^2b - b^3\right)i\). Comparing with \(x + iy\): \(x = a\left(a^2 - 3b^2\right)\) and \(y = b\left(3a^2 - b^2\right)\). Hence \(\dfrac{x}{a} + \dfrac{y}{b} = \left(a^2 - 3b^2\right) + \left(3a^2 - b^2\right) = 4a^2 - 4b^2\). Answer: \(\dfrac{x}{a} + \dfrac{y}{b} = 4\left(a^2 - b^2\right)\)

Cross-multiplying, \(a + 3i = (1 - i)(2 + ib) = 2 + ib - 2i - i^2b = (2 + b) + (b - 2)i\). Equating imaginary parts: \(b - 2 = 3\), so \(b = 5\). Equating real parts: \(a = 2 + b = 7\). Then \(5a - 7b = 5(7) - 7(5) = 35 - 35\). Answer: \(5a - 7b = 0\)

Squaring both sides, \((x + iy)^2 = \dfrac{a + ib}{c + id}\). Taking modulus and using \(\left|z_1/z_2\right| = \left|z_1\right|/\left|z_2\right|\): \(|x + iy|^2 = \dfrac{|a + ib|}{|c + id|}\), that is \(x^2 + y^2 = \dfrac{\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}}{\sqrt{c^2 + d^2}}\). Squaring once more gives the result. Answer: \(\left(x^2 + y^2\right)^2 = \dfrac{a^2 + b^2}{c^2 + d^2}\)

Simplify the right side: \(\dfrac{1 + i}{1 - i} = \dfrac{(1+i)^2}{(1-i)(1+i)} = \dfrac{2i}{2} = i\). So \(a + ib = 0 + 1i\), giving \(a = 0\) and \(b = 1\), hence \(a^2 + b^2 = 0 + 1\). Answer: \(a^2 + b^2 = 1\)

Let \(z = \sqrt{7} + i\sqrt{3}\), so the expression is \(\dfrac{z}{\overline{z}} + \dfrac{\overline{z}}{z} = \dfrac{z^2 + \overline{z}^2}{z\overline{z}}\). Here \(z^2 = 7 + 2\sqrt{21}\,i + 3i^2 = 4 + 2\sqrt{21}\,i\) and \(\overline{z}^2 = 4 - 2\sqrt{21}\,i\), so \(z^2 + \overline{z}^2 = 8\), while \(z\overline{z} = 7 + 3 = 10\). The value \(\dfrac{8}{10}\) has imaginary part \(0\), so the expression is real. Answer: \(\dfrac{4}{5}\), a real number

Expand the cube and separate the parts: \((x + iy)^3 = x^3 + 3x^2(iy) + 3x(iy)^2 + (iy)^3 = \left(x^3 - 3xy^2\right) + \left(3x^2y - y^3\right)i\). Comparing with \(u + vi\) gives \(u = x\left(x^2 - 3y^2\right)\) and \(v = y\left(3x^2 - y^2\right)\). Hence \(\dfrac{u}{x} + \dfrac{v}{y} = \left(x^2 - 3y^2\right) + \left(3x^2 - y^2\right) = 4x^2 - 4y^2\). Answer: \(\dfrac{u}{x} + \dfrac{v}{y} = 4\left(x^2 - y^2\right)\)

Group the parts: \((x + 2y) + (2x - 3y + 4)i = 5 + 0i\). Real parts: \(x + 2y = 5\). Imaginary parts: \(2x - 3y + 4 = 0\), i.e. \(2x - 3y = -4\). Substituting \(x = 5 - 2y\) gives \(10 - 7y = -4\), so \(y = 2\) and then \(x = 1\). Answer: \(x = 1\), \(y = 2\)

Multiply throughout by \((1+i)(1-i) = 2\): \((x+1)(1-i) + (y-1)(1+i) = 2i\). Real parts: \((x+1) + (y-1) = 0\), i.e. \(x + y = 0\). Imaginary parts: \(-(x+1) + (y-1) = 2\), i.e. \(y - x = 4\). Adding the two gives \(2y = 4\). Answer: \(x = -2\), \(y = 2\)

Since \(i^3 = -i\), the equation becomes \((x + 2y - 5) + (3x - y - 1)i = 0 + 0i\). Real parts: \(x + 2y = 5\). Imaginary parts: \(3x - y = 1\), so \(y = 3x - 1\). Substituting, \(x + 2(3x - 1) = 5\), giving \(7x = 7\), so \(x = 1\) and \(y = 2\). Answer: \(x + y = 3\)

Since \(i^6 = i^2 = -1\) and \(i^3 = -i\), the equation becomes \((x - 15y) + 2i = 7x - (y + 4)i\). Imaginary parts: \(2 = -(y + 4)\), so \(y = -6\). Real parts: \(x - 15y = 7x\), i.e. \(-6x = 15y = -90\), so \(x = 15\). Answer: \(x + y = 15 + (-6) = 9\)
